$comment: THE hand-written part. Four packages -- ui, js, php, py -- are generated from this directory and are never edited. Facts read from Twilio's own OpenAPI (github.com/twilio/twilio-oai, spec/json/twilio_api_v2010.json) on 2026-11-08.
title: Twilio
summary: Send SMS with Twilio from a workflow or a Laravel app, and read a message's delivery status.

authorize.$comment: HTTP basic, two parts: an API key SID and its secret (recommended), or the Account SID and its Auth Token. Either way the ACCOUNT SID is also a path segment of every URL (/2010-04-01/Accounts/{AccountSid}/...), which is why it is its own credential rather than read out of the username: with an API key the two differ.

sandboxNote: Twilio's test estate is selected by the CREDENTIALS, not the URL: a separate test Account SID and test Auth Token (Console -> API keys & tokens), against the same api.twilio.com. A live key on a node marked sandbox texts a real phone and is billed. With test credentials only message_send works -- every other resource, including message_get, answers 403 -- nothing is sent or charged, no status callback fires, and From must be Twilio's magic +15005550006 (+15005550004 as To returns 21610, the STOP case). Test credentials are the test Account SID and Auth Token, not an API key.

credentialFields.label: Account SID
credentialFields.help: AC followed by 32 hex characters, from the Twilio Console. It is part of every request URL.

credentialFields.label: API key SID (or Account SID)
credentialFields.help: An API key SID from the Twilio Console (API keys & tokens), recommended. Or the Account SID again, to authenticate with the Auth Token.

credentialFields.label: API key secret (or Auth Token)
credentialFields.help: The secret shown once when the API key was created, or the account's Auth Token. The Auth Token can do everything on the account; an API key can be revoked on its own.

notificationChannel.$comment: PS Mapper: a Laravel Notification sent with via(): ['twilio'] runs message_send. The notifiable's routeNotificationForTwilio() gives `to`; toTwilio() returns the body as a string, or message_send's config as an array (e.g. from, messagingServiceSid, statusCallback).

$setupComment: Every step read from twilio.com/docs on 2026-11-08 (each step cites its page). Not stated by those pages, so not claimed here: that the API key secret is shown only once, and the US carrier error code for unregistered 10DLC traffic.

setup.title: Find your Account SID
setup.detail: Sign in to the Twilio Console; the Account SID is on the Console home page. It is AC followed by 32 hex characters, and it is part of every URL this connector calls. A TRIAL account can only send to verified numbers (up to 5; your sign-up number is verified already), so upgrade before sending to anyone else.

setup.title: Create a Standard API key for {{appName}}
setup.detail: Console: Settings, Account settings, API keys & auth tokens, then Create API key. Choose Standard: it reaches every API this connector uses, but not the Accounts or Keys resources, so it cannot create more keys if it leaks. Copy the key's SID into the username and its secret into the password, and store the secret immediately. Leave the region at the default unless your account uses another Twilio region: this connector calls api.twilio.com.

setup.title: Give {{appName}} a sender
setup.detail: Either a Twilio phone number with SMS capability, or a Messaging Service (Console: Messaging, Services, Create Messaging Service, then add your numbers to its sender pool). message_send takes one of From or MessagingServiceSid; for Laravel notifications set TWILIO_FROM or TWILIO_MESSAGING_SERVICE_SID so a notification that names no sender still has one.

setup.title: Register for A2P 10DLC before texting US numbers
setup.detail: Anyone sending application SMS to the US from a 10-digit long code must register for A2P 10DLC, hobbyists included, and unregistered traffic incurs additional carrier fees. If the number only sends verification codes, Twilio Verify can be used instead of registering.

setup.title: Send a test message and read it back
setup.detail: Send one SMS to a phone you can read, then read it back with message_get to see what Twilio did with it.
setup.prompt: Using {{appName}}'s {{connector}} connection, send one SMS with message_send to a phone the person can read (on a trial account, a verified number), then call message_get with the returned sid and report its status, error_code and error_message.
setup.done: message_get reports status sent or delivered with error_code null, and the person received the text.
